_about: Real NAMASTE / WHO-SAT / ICD-11 codes for MediKiosk (SIH26047). Replaces the TODO placeholders in the demo fixtures.

_provenance.namaste_morbidity: NAMASTE Ayurveda morbidity list, 2910 rows (columns NAMC_ID, NAMC_CODE, NAMC_term, NAMC_term_diacritical, NAMC_term_DEVANAGARI, Name English).
_provenance.who_sat: WHO Standardised International Terminologies for Ayurveda, 12080 rows (columns t_id, Code, parent_id, Word, Short Defination).
_provenance.obtained_from: Public mirrors of both CSVs referenced by github.com/CodexRaunak/NAMASTE-ICD-11-Integration (scripts/download_namaste.py). NOT fetched from the official portal.
_provenance.VERIFY_BEFORE_DEMO: These are mirrors, not the authoritative source. Re-check every code against namaste.ayush.gov.in before this is shown to AIIA. The structure and Devanagari are consistent with the official release, but provenance is second-hand.

_code_format: In the morbidity list a dual-coded row reads 'TM2CODE (NAMC_CODE)' — e.g. 'SP60 (EF-2.4.4)' is ICD-11 TM2 SP60 plus NAMASTE EF-2.4.4. Rows with no parenthetical have no TM2 mapping.

diagnoses.note: Dual-coded in the source. Parent concept pramehaḥ is EF-2 / TM2 SM8D (Polyuria disorder).

There is NO clean NAMASTE→TM2 mapping for essential hypertension. AAE-8 means 'vitiated vāta in rakta', which is a related but not equivalent concept. Do not present this as an equivalence — either have an Ayurveda faculty member confirm the mapping, or code hypertension with the biomedicine code alone. The ICD-11 BA00 code is correct and safe to use.
Subtypes are dual-coded too — vātikajvaraḥ EC-3.2 / TM2 SP54, paittikajvaraḥ EC-3.3 / TM2 SP53.
Dosha subtypes EA-3.2 vāta, EA-3.3 pitta, EA-3.4 kapha are NAMC-only, no TM2 code.
Used by the Meera Krishnan and Farida Sheikh fixtures.

examination_frameworks.note: The framework the problem statement names. It is a leaf node in the SAT list — the ten axes are not enumerated beneath it, they live as general concepts elsewhere in the terminology.

assessment_axes._warning: Several Dashavidha axis names are homonyms of unrelated Ayurvedic concepts in the SAT list. Sara as a Dashavidha axis means tissue excellence; SAT-A.155 saraḥ/calaḥ means 'instability/mobility' and is a guṇa, not the axis. Sattva as an axis means mental strength; SAT-A.127 sattvam is the triguṇa 'purity or goodness'. Those two are left uncoded on purpose rather than mapped to a homonym — a wrong code is worse than no code in front of an Ayurveda panel.

pramana.note: SAT-A.277 pramāṇam is a different sense — 'means of acquiring knowledge'. Use SAT-B.513.

vyayama_shakti.note: Codes the activity, not the capacity (śakti). SAT-I.52 and SAT-I.126 are therapeutic senses — do not use those.

sara.note: Homonym risk — see _warning. Needs an Ayurveda faculty decision.

samhanana.note: No clean standalone entry found in the SAT list.

ahara_shakti.note: No entry for āhāraśakti as a compound. Agni (SAT-B.488) is the closest related concept but is not the same axis.

prakriti.note: Entry exists but carries no definition in the source, so the sense cannot be confirmed from the data alone.

nidra.note: SAT-D.4374 nidrā carries no definition — use SAT-J.3.
